reviews.decision_reason: demand_selection admits every supplied row because it selects demand_score >= 3 and all corpus rows meet that threshold, while the supplied evidence contains only scored need statements rather than observed jobs, pain, triggers, alternatives, consequences, and outcomes. This causes unsupported or weak demand claims such as n06-r01 and n06-r07 to pass into the handoff, enabling the downstream recommendation to prioritize an unsupported top need.

evidence_normalization retains all allowed record ids and applies an eight-row window, so it preserves the faulty selected set instead of making missing demand evidence visible. The unit is not the first source of the bad selection, but it contributes by allowing unsupported records through normalization unchanged.

provenance_assembly deterministically ranks by demand_score, which makes n06-r01 rank first even though the package marks that need unsupported downstream and supplies no market-demand evidence beyond scored background rows. The ranking is deterministic and the exact evidence_sources handoff is preserved, but the ranking criterion is insufficient under the strict market-demand review criteria.
